questions.question: Can I put OFFICIAL data into Microsoft 365 Copilot?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. It is an enterprise tool in the Defra tenant, and OFFICIAL is allowed there with no extra condition.

questions.question: Can I put OFFICIAL data into ChatGPT?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, but only with privacy settings on, which means model training and chat history turned off. The condition must appear.

questions.question: What can I put into a public AI tool?
questions.expected_answer: Public or open information, and OFFICIAL with privacy settings on. Not OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE, not personal data, not SECRET.

questions.question: Is OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE allowed in any AI tool?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, in an enterprise tool inside the Defra tenant. No in a public tool and no in a Defra-hosted one.

questions.question: Can I use SECRET data with AI?
questions.expected_answer: No, in any tool type.

questions.question: Can I use personal data with Microsoft 365 Copilot?
questions.expected_answer: Not for everyday work. A DPIA is required before use, and the DPIA route is for a service being built to process personal data, not for pasting into a tool. The second half of that rule must appear.

questions.question: Do I need a DPIA to use AI?
questions.expected_answer: Two different answers depending on whether they are building a service that processes personal data or using a tool day to day.

questions.question: What is the difference between a public, enterprise and Defra-hosted tool?
questions.expected_answer: Public is a consumer tool on the open web. Enterprise runs inside the Defra tenant. Defra-hosted runs on infrastructure Defra controls.

questions.question: Can I use my own laptop for AI work?
questions.expected_answer: Public or OFFICIAL only. OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE and personal data need a Defra laptop or virtual desktop, through Microsoft 365 Copilot in the Defra environment.

questions.question: What counts as personal data?
questions.expected_answer: Anything that could identify a specific individual, alone or combined with other data.

questions.question: Do I have to take personal data out before I put something in a tool?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, and it is non-negotiable. Quote the rule.

questions.question: Whose job is it to check personal data has gone?
questions.expected_answer: The team's. Someone on the team must verify the output before it enters the pipeline or gets committed to version control.

questions.question: Can source code contain personal data?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. Test fixtures, config and connection strings can all carry it.

questions.question: I found personal data in an AI output. What now?
questions.expected_answer: Follow the incident steps: stop, change nothing, tell your line manager and information asset owner.

questions.question: Can I paste a spreadsheet of names into Copilot to summarise it?
questions.expected_answer: No. Remove the personal data first. Quote the non-negotiable rule.

questions.question: Where does my data go when I use an AI tool?
questions.expected_answer: It depends on the tool type, which is why the tool type determines what you can put in.

questions.question: Is it alright if I use initials instead of full names?
questions.expected_answer: No page covers pseudonymisation. It must not improvise, and it must not reason by analogy from the screenshot rule.

questions.question: What do I do if I am not sure whether something is allowed?
questions.expected_answer: Stop and check before using the tool.

questions.question: Is GitHub Copilot approved?
questions.expected_answer: Status is not approval. You can use any AI tool as long as you follow the data rules. GitHub Copilot's status is Using, which means teams across Defra use it today.

questions.question: Can I use a tool that is not on the radar?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. A tool not on the radar is not banned, it just has not been looked at. Talk to the AI Capability and Enablement team for advice.

questions.question: Is Cursor allowed?
questions.expected_answer: Not on the radar, which does not mean banned. The data rules still apply.

questions.question: What does Trialling mean on the radar?
questions.expected_answer: Being trialled with some teams before wider use.

questions.question: Does a tool's radar status tell me whether I am allowed to use it?
questions.expected_answer: No. Status tells you how established a tool is at Defra, not whether you are allowed to use it. Quote that sentence.

questions.question: How do I choose a tool for my team?
questions.expected_answer: Four steps: check you need AI at all, check the radar, check what data you can use, turn privacy settings on.

questions.question: Is AI already in tools I use without me knowing?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. It is built into tools teams already have, so the data rules apply even when nobody chose to use AI.

questions.question: Is MCP approved for general use?
questions.expected_answer: No, it is not approved for general use. Any use needs written approval from the Project Architect and the AI Capability and Enablement team.

questions.question: What is retrieval-augmented generation?
questions.expected_answer: Giving a model your own documents to answer from, rather than relying on what it was trained on. Status Exploring.

questions.question: Should we use MCP in production?
questions.expected_answer: No. Not approved for general use, and any use needs written approval from two named parties.

questions.question: Which is better, GitHub Copilot or Claude?
questions.expected_answer: No page compares tools against each other.

questions.question: Can I use AWS Bedrock instead of Azure AI Foundry?
questions.expected_answer: Both are Trialling. Neither is a default, and status is not permission.

questions.question: Should I trust code an AI writes?
questions.expected_answer: No. A human review of AI-generated code remains essential.

questions.question: Does AI code need a second reviewer?
questions.expected_answer: For security-critical paths, yes, a second reviewer is required.

questions.question: Can AI output trigger an action in another system?
questions.expected_answer: Never let raw AI output trigger a privileged action on its own.

questions.question: How do I stop AI coding tools reading our secrets?
questions.expected_answer: Configure the tool to exclude secrets, and check for credentials that are already embedded in the code.

questions.question: Can prompt injection be fixed?
questions.expected_answer: No, it cannot be fully fixed. Reduce its impact rather than trying to eliminate it.

questions.question: Do I need static analysis on AI-generated code?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, and dependency scanning as well.

questions.question: Can I let an agent run commands without approving them?
questions.expected_answer: Never auto-approve actions. Keep a human in the loop and review tool calls before they run.

questions.question: Is it safe to give an AI agent access to our repository?
questions.expected_answer: Depends on their environment and what the agent can reach.

questions.question: How do I protect my development environment?
questions.expected_answer: Covered by the section on it, alongside secret handling and dependency scanning.

questions.question: Has Defra been breached through an AI tool?
questions.expected_answer: Not something the toolkit covers, and not ours to answer.

questions.question: I pasted customer data into ChatGPT by mistake. What do I do?
questions.expected_answer: Stop using the AI tool immediately. Do not delete or change anything. Tell your line manager and your team's information asset owner. Report it through your organisation's security incident process. All four steps must appear.

questions.question: Should I delete the chat if I made a mistake?
questions.expected_answer: No. Do not delete or change anything, because the people handling the incident need to see what happened.

questions.question: Will I get in trouble for reporting an incident?
questions.expected_answer: No. You will not be penalised for reporting in good faith, and the risk of not reporting is far greater than the risk of over-reporting.

questions.question: What counts as an AI incident?
questions.expected_answer: The named list, including data going somewhere it should not and acting on a wrong output.

questions.question: I pasted a spreadsheet of names into Copilot. Who do I tell?
questions.expected_answer: Line manager and the team's information asset owner, then the security incident process.

questions.question: What happens after I report?
questions.expected_answer: Your line manager and information asset owner assess how serious it is and decide whether to escalate.

questions.question: An AI gave me wrong information and I acted on it. Is that an incident?
questions.expected_answer: Depends whether data was exposed or a decision was affected.

questions.question: Do I need to tell the Information Commissioner?
questions.expected_answer: A legal determination, not theirs to make alone.

questions.question: What should I know before building a chatbot?
questions.expected_answer: The service must assume sensitive information could be submitted at any time, because we cannot fully control what users type in. There is no fast route to the data access permissions and assurance an open-ended assistant needs, including a DPIA.

questions.question: How do I cut the cost of AI calls?
questions.expected_answer: Prompt compression can cut input tokens by 20 to 60%. Protect instructions and queries, compress the content between them.

questions.question: Did prompt compression work?
questions.expected_answer: Partly. It cut input tokens, but models produced longer responses when given compressed prompts, which offset some of the saving. Measure total tokens, not just input.

questions.question: Which compression method was better?
questions.expected_answer: Caveman compression retained higher output quality than LLMLingua-2. LLMLingua-2 compressed slightly more.

questions.question: What are agent swarms?
questions.expected_answer: The pattern of several agents working together, with the trade-offs the page sets out.

questions.question: How do I work safely with AI agents?
questions.expected_answer: The guidance page sets the rules, and the MCP rules apply to any project trialling it.

questions.question: What is green summarisation?
questions.expected_answer: The pattern for cutting the energy cost of summarising.

questions.question: Should I build my own agent framework or use one?
questions.expected_answer: A decision about their own service.

questions.question: What is the best architecture for my service?
questions.expected_answer: Depends entirely on their service. Must not recommend one.

questions.question: Can an AI agent talk to another AI agent?
questions.expected_answer: Agent-to-Agent covers it. Status Exploring.

questions.question: Do I need to publish a transparency record?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, if the tool significantly influences a decision with public effect, or interacts directly with the public.

questions.question: Do I need to tell people when content was written by AI?
questions.expected_answer: Ethics covers transparency about AI in services, not labelling AI-drafted content. Must not extrapolate.

questions.question: Why does public trust matter for AI?
questions.expected_answer: Government services depend on it, and AI introduces new ways to lose it through unexplainable decisions, biased outputs or mishandled data.

questions.question: Does a bigger model use more energy?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, larger models use more per request.

questions.question: How does Defra decide which AI ideas to take forward?
questions.expected_answer: A panel scores requests against set criteria. Must not mention funding or budget, which the page does not cover.

questions.question: How do I get my AI idea looked at?
questions.expected_answer: Through the triage.
